text: You told ChatGPT you're vegetarian. Open any other AI app, and it has no idea.
And the memory ChatGPT does keep lives on OpenAI's side. Its own help page says ChatGPT decides what to use.
So today you pick one: start from zero in every app, or let one company keep a file on you.
Satchel is the third option. The memory of your assistant goes where you go, and only the apps you allow can read it.
Meet Pip, an AI assistant. Tell it you're vegetarian. Pip locks that fact with your passkey, the fingerprint or face unlock your phone already uses.
What gets stored is scrambled. Without your passkey, it is noise.
Now try Fern, a different AI app, built by someone else. It knows nothing about you.
So you give Fern a grant: a permission slip, posted on Monad, a public record that any app can check and no app can fake.
Ask Fern to plan your weekend. Vegetarian food, a flight out of Bangalore. You never told Fern a thing.
Now change your mind. Tap ree-voke Fern. Pip relocks every memory under a brand new lock.

text: Fern's permission slip opened the old lock. That lock is gone.
Ask Fern again. Generic answer, none of your facts. Fern didn't promise to forget. It simply can't open them any more.
Both taps are real, public records on Monad, each done in seconds.
Any app can add this with one install: lock, grant, take back.
Your AI's memory follows you to any app you allow, and one tap takes it back. Try it at satchel dash keys dot ver cell dot app.
